They davened with all their might for a brocha for children, and that is exactly what happened. Nine months later, almost exactly to the day, on Tes Zayin Shvat 5776, I was born! You can’t imagine what a simcha it was!

I am so grateful to the Rebbe for answering Tatty and Mommy’s tefillos. We are so lucky to be chassidim of the Rebbe who cares so much about us! Let’s do as many mitzvos as we can to make the Rebbe proud!

It was already a few years after their chasunah, and Tatty and Mommy still didn’t have any children. When would they hold a baby of their own?

On Chol Hamoed Sukkos 5775, Tatty bumped into a friend. This friend had been married for more than five years and didn’t have any children. As they spoke, his friend shared amazing news: After so many years of waiting, they finally had a baby on the way!

“It’s all thanks to the Rebbe’s brochos!” his friend said happily. “Last Lag Ba’omer, I went to the Ohel with some mekuravim from my mivtzoyim route. On the way, I discussed with them how Lag Ba’omer is a special day to go to the Ohel and daven for children. They said that they would daven for me! When we got to the Ohel, I asked the Rebbe for a brocha for children, and they davened for me as well. Soon after Lag Ba’omer, we found out that we were expecting!

“When I shared the good news with the mekuravim from my mivtzoyim route, one of them said, ‘the brocha came from Lag Ba’omer!’. Even the mekuravim realized that the brocha came from the Rebbe!”

Tatty was thrilled to hear the good news. “You know,” he said thoughtfully, “going to the Ohel on Lag Ba’omer and davening for children is important and special. But if you bring along someone else who otherwise wouldn’t go, that makes it really special!”

Tatty felt that his friend merited to have a baby because he brought along the mekuravim from his mivtzoyim route. Right then and there, he decided to do the same thing! Next Lag Ba’omer, he would take someone along with him to the Ohel and they would daven for a brocha for children. Tatty and Mommy hoped that in that zechus, they would finally merit the brocha of having a child of their own.
